speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The quota helps to maintain the Singaporean character of our HDB heartlands.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I raised this question because in my house visits, I had observed where there is a certain demographic of residents in certain flats.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Some residents had also given their feedback about their observations in certain flats where you see a certain number of residents of a certain ethnicity.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: In light of that, I am just wondering what happens in situations where the rental is not actually approved by HDB, how are inspections and enforcement done in those situations?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: In a situation where there is non-compliance, what are the specific sanctions or penalties that are given for non-compliance?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: If there are any residents who have observed a certain trend in a particular estate, what recourse do they have in terms of referring this matter to the HDB?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We do enforcement, surprise inspections even, and we will take these errant flat owners to task, as I mentioned earlier.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In putting in place these quotas, I think we also have to bear in mind and calibrate it carefully because there will be genuine flat owners who want to let out their flats and earn some extra income.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If we tighten it too much, then they will find it difficult to rent out their flats, and that may deprive them of some income for their families and households.
